title: Filter form controls have no programmatic label across most data tabs
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (also 2.4.6) AA
description: The county <select> and From/To date inputs are repeated across tabs with no aria-label, no <label for>, and no association to any visible text — a screen-reader user hears an unnamed combobox and two unnamed, indistinguishable date fields. Locations: LifeList.tsx:616 (county select), :644 and :658 (date from/to); BreedingCodeList.tsx:376, :408, :424 (same trio); SpeciesDetail.tsx:604, :629, :643 (same trio). Related instances where a VISIBLE label exists but is not programmatically associated: MapExplorer.tsx:853 (species select), :872 (county select), :896 (media select) and :862/:864 (date text inputs) — their 'Species'/'County'/'Media'/'Date Range' headings are SidebarLabel <div>s (map/MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43), so the selects have no accessible name and the two free-text date inputs are distinguishable only by the placeholder 'YYYY-MM-DD' (format instruction also vanishes once filled — 3.3.2); Settings.tsx:1214, :1226, :1238 (Latitude/Longitude/Radius number inputs whose labels are plain <div>s at :1213/:1225/:1237); ChecklistComparer.tsx:350-353 ('Checklist A/B' <label> elements with no htmlFor, so the inputs' name falls back to the example-URL placeholder). Checklists.tsx:629-663 does this correctly (aria-label="Protocol"/"County"/"From date"/"To date"), proving the house pattern exists.
fix: Match the Checklists.tsx pattern: add aria-label ("County", "From date", "To date") to the bare selects/date inputs in LifeList, BreedingCodeList, SpeciesDetail. In MapExplorer, render SidebarLabel as a <label htmlFor> (or add aria-label to each control), and give the two date inputs distinct names ("Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)" / "Date to (YYYY-MM-DD)"). In Settings, convert the Latitude/Longitude/Radius caption <div>s to <label htmlFor> with input ids. In ChecklistComparer, add htmlFor/id to the existing <label> elements.

verdict.reasoning: Verified every cited location in current code: LifeList/BreedingCodeList/SpeciesDetail county selects and date inputs have no aria-label/label/title; MapExplorer's SidebarLabel is a bare <div> (MapSidebarUI.tsx:35-43) so its selects are unnamed and the two text date inputs share the identical 'YYYY-MM-DD' placeholder; Settings lat/lon/radius captions are plain <div>s; ChecklistComparer's <label> has no htmlFor and doesn't wrap the input. Checklists.tsx really does carry the aria-label house pattern the fix cites, and ACCESSIBILITY.md discloses only chart-label contrast as a known exception, not this. Serious is the right severity — repeated unnamed form controls across most data tabs is a genuine 4.1.2/1.3.1 SR barrier, though the controls remain operable.
verdict.fixNote: The fix is correct and convention-consistent (mirror Checklists.tsx's aria-label="County"/"From date"/"To date"). One caveat: do not unconditionally convert SidebarLabel to <label htmlFor> — it also captions the Breeding Code SegControl, a button group with no labelable element. Either add aria-label per control in MapExplorer (including format-bearing names like 'Date from (YYYY-MM-DD)' on the free-text date inputs), or give SidebarLabel an optional htmlFor prop that renders <label> only when an id is passed.

title: Selected state not programmatically exposed on segmented controls and toggle pills
description: The shared SegControl renders plain <button>s whose active option is conveyed only by background/border/font-weight — no aria-pressed, aria-checked, or radiogroup semantics. It is used for the Map Explorer radius (MapExplorer.tsx:700), breeding filter (:881), Pins/Heatmap display mode (:912), and All/Week (:1285). The same style-only-state defect appears in SpeciesDetail.tsx:1189 (Pins/Heatmap map-mode buttons), BirdingStats.tsx:541 (accumulation granularity), :1628 (breeding filter pills), :1717 (media view mode), ListComparer.tsx:215 (My List / Upload source buttons), and MapExplorer.tsx:1030 (hotspot kind-legend toggles, whose only state cue is opacity 0.4). A screen-reader user cannot tell which option is active. This directly contradicts ACCESSIBILITY.md: "Filter pills announce whether they are pressed." The codebase already has the correct pattern (SortSeg in Checklists.tsx:74, SnowMap.tsx:144, SpeciesDetail graph groups :962/:974).
fix: Add aria-pressed={value === opt.value} (or role="radio"/aria-checked inside a role="radiogroup") to SegControl's buttons and to each listed location; wrap each group in role="group" with an aria-label.

verdict.reasoning: SegControl (MapSidebarUI.tsx:15-29) renders plain buttons with style-only active state, and every cited usage checks out: MapExplorer 700/881/912/1285, SpeciesDetail ~1189, BirdingStats 541/1628/1717, ListComparer 215, and the hotspot kind-legend toggles at MapExplorer 1030 whose only state cue is opacity 0.4. The correct pattern does exist in SortSeg (Checklists.tsx, role=group + aria-pressed) and SnowMap.tsx:144, and ACCESSIBILITY.md's 'filter pills announce whether they are pressed' claim is contradicted rather than disclosed as an exception. Serious is fair: a screen-reader user cannot determine the active option on roughly ten primary filter/view controls.
verdict.fixNote: Give SegControl an ariaLabel prop rendered as role="group" aria-label on its wrapper div plus aria-pressed={value === opt.value} on each button, mirroring SortSeg in Checklists.tsx (the SidebarLabel above it is not programmatically associated, so the group needs its own label). Apply the same aria-pressed to the inline groups in SpeciesDetail, BirdingStats, and ListComparer; for the kind-legend visibility toggles use aria-pressed={!isHidden} so pressed means shown.

title: Media Targets keyboard path is partial and ACCESSIBILITY.md overstates it
description: Media Target chips are DOM <Marker>s with a click-only <div> (no tabindex/role), so the chips themselves are not operable by keyboard. The only keyboard route to a target popup is the 'Nearest Targets' list (MapExplorer.tsx:1292-1338), which is hard-capped at 10 items sorted by distance from the SEARCH CENTER (nearest10 useMemo, MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) — it is not scoped to the map viewport, does not update on pan/zoom, and shows no over-cap hint. Any target beyond the nearest 10 (easy with a 25-50 mi radius) has no keyboard path at all. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 claims "The Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list works the same way" and that "These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom" — that is true for sightings/hotspots (cap 200, BoundsTracker-driven) but false for targets, so the published statement is currently inaccurate.
fix: Render an InViewMarkerList for targets like the other two modes (items = locationGroups filtered by mapBounds via markersInView, cap 200 with the over-cap hint), keeping 'Nearest Targets' as a convenience list; or at minimum correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center, not viewport-scoped.

verdict.reasoning: Verified TargetMarkers.tsx:69-75: chips are click-only divs with no tabindex/role, and MapExplorer.tsx:453-461 confirms nearest10 is distance-from-search-center, slice(0,10), with no mapBounds dependency — so targets beyond the nearest 10 have no keyboard route at all, unlike sightings/hotspots which use markersInView (cap 200, viewport-driven) into InViewMarkerList. ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13's claim that the targets list 'works the same way' and is 'scoped to the current map view' is factually wrong for this mode. Genuine 2.1.1 Level A gap in a primary feature plus an inaccurate published statement; serious stands.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested InViewMarkerList fix is correct and matches existing conventions, with two precisions: (1) the locId grouping currently lives in TargetMarkers.tsx's locationGroups useMemo, so either lift it to MapExplorer (shared with displayedTargetPins) or recompute it there before feeding markersInView, and wire onActivate to the existing setSelectedTargetLocId + setPanTarget pair (same owner the chip click uses); (2) per CLAUDE.md, update ACCESSIBILITY.md in the same change — either to truthfully describe the viewport-scoped list once built, or immediately to state that the targets list is the nearest 10 from the search center.

title: Species Detail / Named Birds map pins (DOM markers) have no keyboard access path
description: The shared SightingsMap renders each sighting pin as a react-map-gl <Marker> whose content is a plain <div> with a click handler routed through Marker onClick — no tabIndex, no role, no keydown handler — so a keyboard user can never open the per-coordinate popup. On Species Detail ("Sighting Locations" map) that popup is the ONLY place exposing the per-sighting checklist links for sightings without comments (Top Locations rows at SpeciesDetail.tsx:1122-1137 show only name+count; the Comments section only covers commented sightings), so those eBird links are pointer-only functionality. Same pattern, lower impact (keyboard equivalents exist nearby): TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 chip markers (mitigated by the sidebar "Nearest Targets" locate buttons opening the same popup) and BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 geographic-stats rank pins (popup content fully duplicated in the adjacent "Top locations" text lists). Named Birds card maps are also unreachable but each row already lists every sighting's checklist link (NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100). Note ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim covers only the Map Explorer GL markers; these DOM-marker maps have no equivalent of its in-view lists.
fix: DOM markers CAN be focusable (unlike the GL pins): make the marker content a <button aria-label={locName + ' — N sightings'}> so Tab+Enter opens the popup, or reuse the Map Explorer pattern (a focusable list of coordinates that drives the same selectedCoord state). For Species Detail specifically, alternatively surface the per-coordinate checklist links in the keyboard-reachable Top Locations rows.

verdict.reasoning: Verified SightingsMap.tsx:54-58 (and TargetMarkers.tsx, BirdingStats.tsx:862-872): pins are plain div Marker children with click wired through react-map-gl's native click listener; maplibre only adds tabindex/keypress via setPopup(), which this code never uses, so no pin is focusable or keyboard-activatable. The Species Detail impact claim checks out — Top Locations rows (SpeciesDetail.tsx:1115-1138) show name+count only and the Comments section filters to commented sightings (line 372), so checklist links for uncommented sightings are popup-only, i.e. pointer-only. ACCESSIBILITY.md's keyboard-alternative claim is explicitly Map Explorer-scoped and its only disclosed exception is chart-label contrast, so this Level A lockout is undisclosed; serious is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The button-child fix needs no custom keydown handler: react-map-gl attaches a native click listener to the marker wrapper, so Enter/Space on a real <button aria-label={`${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`}> child dispatches a click that bubbles to it. One refinement: maplibre's Marker.addTo() already stamps the wrapper div with role='button' + generic aria-label='Map marker', so via the Marker ref call marker.getElement().setAttribute('role','presentation') and removeAttribute('aria-label') to avoid a nested-button announcement (or instead set the descriptive aria-label + tabindex on the wrapper itself through the ref and skip the inner button). Apply the same treatment to TargetMarkers.tsx and the BirdingStats rank pins; the Species Detail alternative (links in Top Locations rows) should reuse the existing NamedBirdRow.tsx aria-label pattern for checklist anchors.

title: Dark theme: white chip/badge text on lightened recency-tier fills fails badly (1.52–1.92:1)
description: tierColors() hardcodes text:'white' for the fresh and mid recency tiers, but the dark-theme tokens lighten those fills (--sr-map-target-fresh #34D399, --sr-map-target-mid #6EE7B7). Computed: white on #34D399 = 1.92:1, white on #6EE7B7 = 1.52:1 (dark); even light-theme mid (#5EA07C) is only 3.09:1. These colors carry the species-name label on every Media Targets map chip (TargetMarkers.tsx:72, 11px/600) and the '≤7 days' tier badge in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:100, 10px/600) — the primary content of the Map Explorer's Media Targets mode is near-unreadable in dark mode. The 'old' tier already does this right (--sr-map-target-old-text adapts per theme, 4.86:1 light / 10.83:1 dark).
fix: Add per-tier text tokens like the existing --sr-map-target-old-text (e.g. --sr-map-target-fresh-text / -mid-text: white in light where the fill is dark enough, dark green like #052E16 in dark where the fills are pastel) and return them from tierColors() instead of the literal 'white'.

verdict.reasoning: Re-ran WCAG math: white on dark-theme #34D399 = 1.92:1 and #6EE7B7 = 1.52:1 (light-theme mid #5EA07C = 3.09:1), all failing 4.5:1 for the 11px/600 chip text (TargetMarkers.tsx:72) and 10px/600 tier badge (line 100) that carry the Media Targets mode's primary content. tierColors() at mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62 hardcodes 'white' while the old tier already uses a per-theme --sr-map-target-old-text token, confirming the asymmetry. ACCESSIBILITY.md's only disclosed contrast exception is chart-bar labels and it claims map popups meet AA, so this is undisclosed; serious is the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested per-tier text tokens are correct and convention-conforming (define in both :root and [data-theme="dark"]); make explicit that --sr-map-target-mid-text must be dark in the LIGHT theme too (white on light-mid #5EA07C is only 3.09:1, failing 4.5:1 at 11px), while --sr-map-target-fresh-text can stay white in light (#2D8653 = 4.52:1) and go dark (e.g. #052E16) in dark.

title: ACCESSIBILITY.md contrast claim is broader than the computed reality
description: The published statement says text, buttons, links, map popups and form controls 'meet the WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standard (4.5:1) in both the light and dark themes', with chart-bar labels as the only known exception. Computed counterexamples outside that exception: light-theme active pills/links on tinted backgrounds 4.03–4.41:1 (accent-on-accent-bg, error-on-error-bg, active tab on page bg), --sr-text-disabled used on content at 2.29–2.56:1, dark-theme target chips at 1.52–1.92:1, dark-theme breeding pills at 1.97–2.94:1, and form-control borders at 1.19–1.27:1 (non-text). The repo treats this file as a published statement whose claims must be true; today it overstates. (Verified-true parts: the tier-1 badge example, the recency-dot hidden labels, the text-footer/sci-name token fixes, focus-ring contrast, and the dark-mode popup theming.)
fix: Either fix the token-level failures in this report (most are 1-line token edits) and keep the claim, or temporarily widen the known-exceptions paragraph to honestly cover active-state tints in light theme and chip/pill labels in dark theme.

verdict.reasoning: Recomputed all cited ratios independently and each one holds with co-occurring real UI: light accent-on-accent-bg 4.03 / error-on-error-bg 4.41 (LifeList.tsx:107-108 active pills) / active tab on bg 4.32 (TabNav.tsx:94); --sr-text-disabled 2.29-2.57 on non-disabled content (Settings.tsx:240/376 sublabels); dark target chips 1.52/1.92 (white text hardcoded in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:61-62); dark breeding pills 1.97-2.94 after alpha-blending the 0.08 tints (BreedingCodeList.tsx:43-60); borders 1.19-1.27. ACCESSIBILITY.md:31 claims AA in both themes with only the chart-bar-label exception, so the published statement is overstated — and CLAUDE.md explicitly requires this file's claims to stay true. The only stated exception does not cover any of these, so alreadyDisclosed is false.
verdict.fixNote: The two-option fix is sound, with one correction: the dark-theme target-chip failure is not a token edit — lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts hardcodes text: 'white' (itself against the no-hardcoded-colors convention). Fix it like the existing old-tier pattern: add --sr-map-target-fresh-text / --sr-map-target-mid-text tokens to BOTH :root and [data-theme="dark"] in globals.css and reference them, mirroring --sr-map-target-old-text. The breeding-pill fix likewise needs the dark-theme tier text colors lightened (or pill text switched to --sr-text) rather than tint-alpha tweaks, since the 0.08 tint barely moves the blended background. Any token change must land in both theme blocks per convention; ACCESSIBILITY.md edits alone need no version bump.

title: Atlas block popups are pointer-only — no keyboard route to open them
description: Atlas block info popups open exclusively via a MapLibre map.on('click','sr-atlas-fill') handler on the GL fill layer (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132). There is no sidebar list, search, or other focusable path to a block, so the popup's content — block name, the eBird atlas portal link, and 'Highest breeding code … N of your breeding records in this block' — is unreachable without a pointer. The breeding data shown in the popup is not surfaced anywhere else in the app (the sidebar legend only explains tier colors). The popup JSX itself is fine (escaped, keeps the default labeled close button), but keyboard users can never open it.
fix: When shading is on, add a focusable 'Shaded blocks in view' sidebar list (mirroring InViewMarkerList — blocksInBounds already provides viewport-scoped blocks and breedingByBlock the per-block data) whose rows open the same popup; or expose a block search/jump input. Cap + hint like the other lists.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the cited handler (AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132) is the sole path to setSel, and grep confirms BlockBreeding/breedingByBlock data is surfaced nowhere else in the app, so the popup content is genuinely pointer-only. The suggested fix matches existing conventions (InViewMarkerList in map/MapSidebarUI.tsx, blocksInBounds viewport scoping, cap+hint pattern) and correctly notes only shaded blocks need listing. Not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md; moderate severity appropriate. (Duplicate of finding 20.)

title: Atlas block popup is only openable by pointer click on the GL fill layer
description: The California atlas block popup (block name, code, and the link to the eBird Atlas portal for that block) opens solely via map.on('click', 'sr-atlas-fill', …) — a canvas hit-test with no DOM focus path. Unlike the sighting pins, hotspots, and targets, there is no keyboard-accessible in-view list for atlas blocks, so the block-details/atlas-portal-link functionality is unavailable without a pointer. The atlas TOGGLE switches themselves are fine (real role="switch" buttons).
fix: Add a capped "Atlas blocks in view" entry path mirroring InViewMarkerList (rows open the same block popup), or at minimum a keyboard-reachable control that opens the block containing the map center. Update ACCESSIBILITY.md's map-markers section accordingly when fixed.

verdict.reasoning: AtlasLayer.tsx:109-132 opens the block popup only via map.on('click','sr-atlas-fill') canvas hit-testing; I verified InViewMarkerList is used solely for sightings (MapExplorer.tsx:943) and hotspots (:1059) and that breedingByBlock is consumed nowhere but this popup, so no keyboard route to the block name, breeding summary, or eBird atlas portal link exists. ACCESSIBILITY.md's map-markers paragraph documents the sightings/hotspots/targets keyboard lists but never mentions atlas blocks, so this is an undisclosed gap. Real 2.1.1 failure; moderate is fair for a supplementary overlay feature. (Duplicate of finding 58.)

title: Map chrome text inherits MapLibre's fixed `font: 12px/20px Helvetica` — does not scale with the in-app Text Size control
description:
maplibre-gl.css (imported at SnowMap.tsx:7) sets `.maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,…}`. The app's `.maplibregl-popup-content` override in globals.css:568 themes colors but sets no font-size or family, so any map-rendered text without an explicit rem size stays at a hard 12px Helvetica regardless of the Text Size setting. Affected: (1) the AtlasLayer block popup title — `
{sel.name}
` at AtlasLayer.tsx:213 and the linked variant at :208-211 have no fontSize; (2) the attribution credits on every map (SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}` — provider links render at fixed 12px when expanded); (3) the AtlasLayer popup's default close button (it is the only popup that doesn't pass `closeButton={false}`, so users get maplibre's small fixed-size '×' — also a WCAG 2.2 2.5.8 Target Size concern). This matters more here than in a typical web app: ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 states the Text Size control is "especially useful in the desktop app, which has no browser zoom of its own", so on desktop this text is genuinely un-resizable. All other popups (SightingMarkers, HotspotMarkers, TargetMarkers, SightingsMap, the BirdingStats geo popup) set explicit rem sizes and are fine.
fix: In globals.css extend the existing popup override: `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`; give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize; pass `closeButton={false}` on the AtlasLayer popup for consistency with the other four popups (its onClose path already exists).

verdict.reasoning: Every claim checks out: maplibre-gl.css sets .maplibregl-map{font:12px/20px Helvetica Neue,...}, the globals.css:568 popup override adds no font-size/family, the AtlasLayer block name (:208-213) has no fontSize, .maplibregl-ctrl-attrib inherits the fixed 12px, and the Text Size control scales only rem text via html{font-size:calc(100% * var(--sr-text-scale))} (globals.css:378). On desktop — which ACCESSIBILITY.md:37 itself says has no browser zoom — this text is un-resizable, a genuine 1.4.4 failure there (web is saved by browser zoom); at 200% the popup title would render smaller than its own muted secondary text. AtlasLayer is indeed the only popup of six without closeButton={false}, but that part of the fix is wrong (see fixNote).
verdict.fixNote: The CSS parts are right: extend the existing globals.css override with `.maplibregl-popup-content { font-size: 0.8125rem; font-family: var(--font-sans); }` and add `.maplibregl-ctrl-attrib { font-size: 0.6875rem; }`, and give the AtlasLayer block-name elements an explicit rem fontSize (e.g. 0.8125rem). But do NOT pass closeButton={false} on the AtlasLayer popup: it also sets closeOnClick={false}, so the default close button is its only dismiss affordance and its only keyboard-operable control — removing it would strand the popup open and worsen 2.1.1. Instead keep the button and size it via the existing .maplibregl-popup-close-button override (e.g. add `font-size: 1rem; padding: 2px 8px;`), which also addresses the 2.5.8 target-size concern.

title: 'Personal Location' popup badge fails in light theme (2.90:1)
description: The hotspot popup's 'Personal Location' badge sets --sr-map-personal (#C9842A) text on --sr-is-target-bg (#FFF7ED): 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 (dark passes, 8.38:1). The pin color token was designed as a map fill, not a text color.
fix: Use --sr-is-target-text (#C2410C, 4.88:1 on that bg) or --sr-warning for the badge text in light theme.

verdict.reasoning: Independently recomputed: #C9842A (--sr-map-personal) on #FFF7ED (--sr-is-target-bg) = 2.90:1 in light theme at 11px/600 — small text, fails the 4.5:1 AA minimum exactly as reported; dark theme (#E0A060 on #1C0F00) = 8.38:1, passes. HotspotMarkers.tsx:156 matches the finding, and the badge is the popup's only textual indicator that the pin is a personal location, so it is meaningful text — moderate stands. Not disclosed: ACCESSIBILITY.md affirmatively claims map popups meet AA and lists only chart-bar percentage labels as the known exception.
verdict.fixNote: Swap color: 'var(--sr-map-personal)' for 'var(--sr-is-target-text)' unconditionally — no light-theme branch needed, since the token is theme-scoped (4.88:1 light, 8.30:1 dark, both pass) and --sr-is-target-bg + --sr-is-target-text is already the codebase's badge pairing (LifeList.tsx:529).

title: Light theme: muted text on tinted surfaces falls just under AA (4.27–4.40:1)
description: --sr-text-muted #71717A passes on white (4.83:1) but not on the tinted surfaces it is commonly paired with in light theme: on --sr-surface-subtle = 4.40:1 (inactive segmented-control labels in MapSidebarUI SegControl, the basemap switcher buttons in globals.css:246, the missing-media badges in the target popup TargetMarkers.tsx:92, numerous chips); on --sr-quote-bg = 4.27:1 (Named Birds comment block); on --sr-accent-bg = 4.31:1 (secondary text inside selected rows, e.g. the location line of a selected Nearest Targets row, MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317). Dark theme passes all three (5.27–5.82:1).
fix: Darken light --sr-text-muted to ~#6B6B74 (≈4.6:1 on #F4F4F5) — a single token change; verify it still reads as 'muted' next to --sr-text.

verdict.reasoning: Independent WCAG math confirms the ratios: #71717A is 4.397:1 on #F4F4F5, 4.268:1 on #EFF1F3, and 4.310:1 on #E8F5EE (dark theme passes 5.27-5.82), and the surface-subtle and accent-bg pairings genuinely co-occur at small text sizes (SegControl inactive labels MapSidebarUI.tsx:13+24, basemap switcher globals.css:234/246, TargetMarkers.tsx:92 badges, selected-row secondary text MapSidebarUI.tsx:96+109 and MapExplorer.tsx:1306+1317); these are enabled controls, so the inactive-component exemption does not apply. One cited pairing is wrong: the quote-bg comment blocks (NamedBirdRow.tsx:110, Checklists.tsx:350-351) use full-contrast --sr-text, not muted, so that instance never occurs — but the finding stands on the other two surfaces. The proposed #6B6B74 verifies as passing everywhere (4.66-4.80 on the tinted surfaces, 5.28 on white), and changing only the :root value is convention-clean since the token already exists in both themes; not covered by ACCESSIBILITY.md's chart-bar-label exception.

title: Map popups cannot be dismissed with the keyboard (no close button, no Escape)
description: Every app-rendered map popup passes closeButton={false}, and MapLibre's Popup has no built-in Escape handling (verified: no keydown/Escape in maplibre-gl/src/ui/popup.ts), so the only dismissal is a pointer click on empty map. The Map Explorer in-view list rows open popups by keyboard (good) but never close them: onActivate always sets the locId (MapExplorer.tsx:504-512) — re-activating a row with aria-pressed="true" does not toggle it off, so the pressed state is also a one-way lie. Affected popups: SightingMarkers.tsx:111, HotspotMarkers.tsx:141, TargetMarkers.tsx:79, SightingsMap.tsx:61, BirdingStats.tsx:875. A stuck-open popup overlays the map and inserts extra tab stops (eBird links inside it). The AtlasLayer popup (AtlasLayer.tsx:205) is the one that keeps the default close button — proving the styled close button is available.
fix: Either re-enable closeButton (MapLibre renders a real <button aria-label="Close popup">, already themed via .maplibregl-popup-content CSS), or add an Escape keydown handler that clears the selection state, and make in-view list rows toggle (activating the already-selected row calls onSelect(null)). Any one of these resolves it; the row toggle also fixes the aria-pressed semantics.

verdict.reasoning: All five cited popups pass closeButton={false} at the exact lines, maplibre-gl's bundle contains zero Escape handling, and MapExplorer's only Escape handler is the mobile-sidebar focus trap — so popups opened via the keyboard-accessible in-view lists (which one-way set locId, never toggling aria-pressed rows off) have no keyboard dismissal at all. The HotspotMarkers popup adds real eBird-link tab stops, making this user-impacting under WCAG 2.1.1. ACCESSIBILITY.md describes the keyboard open path but does not disclose the missing dismissal; the suggested fix is accurate and convention-aligned (AtlasLayer.tsx:205 keeps the default close button, a real <button aria-label="Close popup"> already themed via .maplibregl-popup-close-button with var(--sr-text-muted) in globals.css:576).

title: Missing-media type icons in Media Targets popup and marker chips have no text alternative anywhere
description: The whole point of a media target is which media types (photo/audio/video) the user is missing, but that information is conveyed exclusively by unnamed inline SVGs: in the target popup (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97, bare <svg> per missing type, no aria-hidden, no label), in the on-map chip labels (TargetMarkers.tsx:62, MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), and the keyboard-accessible "Nearest Targets" sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:~1315-1318) show only name/location/distance — they omit missing types entirely. A screen-reader user can find a target but never learn which media it is missing. This also weakens the ACCESSIBILITY.md claim that icon-only information "carries a hidden text label so it is never lost to a screen reader."
fix: In the popup, give each type span role="img" aria-label={`Missing ${t.toLowerCase()}`} (or append sr-only text) and aria-hidden the SVGs; add the missing types as text (visible or sr-only) to the Nearest Targets sidebar rows so the keyboard/SR path carries the full information.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three cited surfaces: popup spans (TargetMarkers.tsx:91-97) hold bare unnamed SVGs with no role/aria-label/sr-only text, chip labels inject raw MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line 62, mapExplorerFormat.ts:30-34) with no ARIA, and the Nearest Targets sidebar rows (MapExplorer.tsx:1315-1319) render only name/location/distance — missingTypes never appears as text on any keyboard/SR path. The type-filter pills filter the set but don't convey per-target info, so the feature's core information is icon-only, contradicting ACCESSIBILITY.md line 19's hidden-label claim. Moderate is the right severity: SR users can reach targets but lose the missing-media detail.
verdict.fixNote: The suggested fix is right; extend it slightly: also add aria-hidden="true" into the three MEDIA_ICONS SVG strings in lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts so browse-mode screen readers don't hit unnamed images on the on-map chips, and for the sidebar rows reuse the existing sr-only span pattern already used for the recency dot at MapExplorer.tsx:1311-1313 (e.g. Missing photo, audio).

title: 'Nearest Targets' list is not scoped to the map view and does not update on pan/zoom, contrary to the statement
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md says the Media Targets mode's 'Nearest Targets' list 'works the same way' as the in-view lists and then asserts 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom (very dense views are capped, with a "zoom in to narrow the list" hint).' The keyboard path itself is real (each row has a focusable, aria-labelled locate button at lines 1320-1333 that opens the same popup and pans). But `nearest10` (lines 453-461) is computed as the 10 closest pins to the SEARCH CENTER lat/lng inputs — it ignores `mapBounds`, never reacts to panning or zooming, and has no over-cap hint. Only the 'Sightings in view' and 'Hotspots in view' lists (markersInView + mapBounds, cap 200, MapSidebarUI.tsx:118-121) match the published description. A screen-reader user following the statement would expect the targets keyboard list to track the viewport; it doesn't.
fix: Either scope the targets list with markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) like the other two lists, or correct ACCESSIBILITY.md to say the targets list is the 10 nearest to the search center.

verdict.reasoning: nearest10 (MapExplorer.tsx:453-461) is sorted by distance from the lat/lng search-center inputs with deps [displayedTargetPins, lat, lng] — it never reads mapBounds, never reacts to pan/zoom, and has no over-cap hint — while ACCESSIBILITY.md line 13 explicitly includes the Nearest Targets list in 'These lists are scoped to the current map view and update as you pan or zoom'. The gap is functional, not just a claims bug: target chips are DOM divs with onClick but no tabIndex (TargetMarkers.tsx), so targets beyond the 10 nearest to the center have no keyboard path at all while mouse users can click any chip. Moderate is fair (false published assistive-behavior claim plus a real 2.1.1 gap).
verdict.fixNote: If scoping to the viewport, reuse the existing pattern rather than patching nearest10: derive markersInView(displayedTargetPins, mapBounds) and render through the shared InViewMarkerList (MapSidebarUI.tsx) like sightingsInView/hotspotsInView, which gives the cap + 'zoom in to narrow the list' hint for free. Otherwise the one-line ACCESSIBILITY.md correction ('the targets list shows the 10 nearest the search center') is the cheaper honest fix.

title: DOM map markers (Species Detail / Named Birds pins, target chips, Statistics rank pins) are unnamed, role-less click targets invisible to AT
wcag: 1.1.1 Non-text Content A / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value A
description: ACCESSIBILITY.md documents sidebar-list alternatives for the Map Explorer's GPU canvas markers, but the DOM <Marker> maps have no equivalent treatment: SightingsMap.tsx:55-58 renders each pin as a clickable <div> containing an innerHTML SVG with no role, name, or tabindex; TargetMarkers.tsx:69-74 does the same for target chips; BirdingStats.tsx:863-872 for the Statistics RankIcon pins (statsPrimitives.tsx:92-101, an unnamed SVG). Screen-reader and keyboard users cannot perceive or activate any of these markers or reach their popups. Impact is moderated because equivalent data exists in adjacent text on most surfaces (Named Birds rows list every sighting date/location/checklist; Species Detail has Top Locations and per-sighting lists; Statistics has top-location tables), but the popup-only details (e.g. per-coordinate date groupings) have no named path.
fix: Make the Marker child a real button: role="button", tabIndex=0, aria-label like `${locName ?? coordinate}, ${sightings.length} sightings` with Enter/Space handling — or explicitly scope the ACCESSIBILITY.md marker claim and guarantee a text equivalent exists beside every DOM-marker map.

verdict.reasoning: The literal 'no role, name' claim is partly wrong — maplibre 5.24's Marker.addTo() (src/ui/marker.ts:340-348) stamps every marker wrapper with role='button' and default aria-label='Map marker' — but the substantive 1.1.1 failure stands: all pins announce identically with no location/count, are not focusable (tabindex comes only from the unused setPopup path), and the popup-only per-coordinate details have no named path. The cited mitigations are real (BirdingStats pins duplicate the adjacent 'Top locations by checklists/species' lists; NamedBirdRow lists every checklist link; TargetMarkers has the Nearest Targets sidebar), so moderate is the right severity. ACCESSIBILITY.md's marker claim is Map Explorer-only and does not disclose this.
verdict.fixNote: Correction to the finding's mechanism: the markers are not role-less/invisible — maplibre already applies role='button' + a generic identical aria-label ('Map marker') to the wrapper, so the defect is a non-descriptive name plus no focusability. Fix by giving each pin a descriptive per-pin name: either set it on the wrapper via the Marker ref (marker.getElement().setAttribute('aria-label', `${locName ?? coord}, ${n} sightings`) plus tabindex='0' — maplibre preserves a pre-set label), or render a real <button aria-label=...> child and demote the wrapper to role='presentation' via the ref to avoid nested-button announcements. The finding's hand-rolled role='button'/tabIndex/Enter-Space div is workable but creates button-inside-button nesting and re-implements what a native <button> gives for free.

title: Rotate/pitch gestures left enabled on all four maps with the compass reset hidden — multipoint-only on touch, no single-pointer alternative or reset, and the app never uses bearing/pitch
description: SnowMap's single MapGL mount (SnowMap.tsx:117) passes no gesture overrides, so maplibre-gl 5.24.0 defaults leave dragRotate, touchZoomRotate (rotation), touchPitch, and pitchWithRotate all enabled — empirically confirmed (handler state dragRotateEnabled/touchPitchEnabled/touchZoomRotateEnabled all true in both embed configs; Shift+ArrowRight rotated bearing to 15°, Shift+ArrowUp pitched to 10°). On touch devices, rotation is a two-finger twist and pitch a two-finger vertical drag — multipoint gestures with no single-pointer alternative: the NavigationControl compass (the standard single-tap bearing/pitch reset) is explicitly hidden (`showCompass={false}`, SnowMap.tsx:125), and no app code ever calls resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch. A touch user who triggers these accidentally is stranded in a rotated/tilted view: the app's fitBounds calls reset bearing only — pitch survives fitBounds (verified empirically: pitch 40° unchanged after fitBounds) — and they are data-driven fits, not user-invocable resets. Desktop right-drag/Ctrl-drag and keyboard Shift+arrows exist but are unavailable to touch single-pointer users. The app itself never uses bearing or pitch, so this is unused functionality left armed on all four map surfaces (Map Explorer, Species Detail, Statistics, SightingsMap/Named Birds). Note: this is distinct from every gesture/keyboard finding already recorded in verified-findings.json (none cover rotation/pitch or the hidden compass).
evidence: SnowMap.tsx:125 `<NavigationControl position="top-left" showCompass={false} />`; grep of frontend/src finds no dragRotate/touchPitch/touchZoomRotate/pitchWithRotate/keyboard props on any mount; maplibre-gl src/ui/map.ts:472-499 defaults `dragRotate: true, touchZoomRotate: true, touchPitch: true, pitchWithRotate: true`; live check: bearing 15°/pitch 10° reached via gestures' keyboard twins, and fitBounds left pitch at 40° (bearing-only reset); no resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch anywhere in app code
suggestedFix: Disable the unused gestures once in SnowMap (covers all four surfaces): pass `dragRotate={false}` `touchPitch={false}` `pitchWithRotate={false}` on the MapGL mount, and call `e.target.touchZoomRotate.disableRotation()` in the map's load handler (this keeps pinch ZOOM working — do not pass `touchZoomRotate={false}`, which would disable pinch zoom too). Do NOT call `map.keyboard.disableRotation()` — in maplibre 5.24 it disables keyboard PAN as well as rotate. Alternative if rotation is ever wanted: restore the compass (`showCompass` default) with `visualizePitch: true` so one tap resets bearing and pitch, providing the single-pointer alternative/reset.

verdict.reasoning: Verified: SnowMap.tsx:117-125 passes no gesture overrides (maplibre-gl 5.24 bundle defaults dragRotate/touchZoomRotate/touchPitch/pitchWithRotate all true), hides the compass (showCompass={false}), and grep of frontend/src finds no resetNorth/setBearing/setPitch anywhere — so rotation/pitch are multipoint-only on touch with no single-pointer alternative or reset, on all four SnowMap-backed surfaces. A touch user who accidentally twists/tilts has no recovery control, which is a fair 2.5.1 failure plus a real stranding hazard; no existing finding in either file covers rotation/pitch or the hidden compass. Moderate is appropriate.
verdict.fixNote: One correction to the suggested fix: maplibre 5.24's keyboard.disableRotation() does NOT disable keyboard pan — it only zeroes the Shift+arrow bearing/pitch deltas (bundle: `_rotationDisabled&&(o=0,a=0)`; plain arrows still pan), so it is safe to call as well. The rest is correct: pass dragRotate={false} touchPitch={false} pitchWithRotate={false} on the MapGL mount and call e.target.touchZoomRotate.disableRotation() in onLoad (keeps pinch zoom); or restore the compass with visualizePitch for a single-tap reset.

title: The same 'open this checklist on eBird' function is identified four different ways across tabs
description: One repeated function — a link that opens a specific checklist on ebird.org — is identified with four different affordances and three different name vocabularies depending on the tab (this is the identification inconsistency itself, distinct from the already-reported missing new-window indication and the ↗ accessible-name weakness): (1) bare '↗' glyph with title="Open checklist" (BirdingStats.tsx:1332, 1564, 1589); (2) data value + lucide ExternalLink icon, no label at all (speciesDetail/ui.tsx:52-78 StatValueLink, Checklists.tsx:48-65 DateLink) — except NamedBirdRow.tsx:91-100, where the identical id+icon link carries aria-label="Open eBird checklist S… (opens in a new tab)"; (3) plain accent-colored text with no icon and no underline, indistinguishable from the adjacent non-link values (BirdingStats.tsx:500, 695, 726, 1448, 1525; SightingsMap.tsx:67 popup dates; map/TargetMarkers.tsx:104); (4) underlined id text with title="View this checklist on eBird" (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). Where a name exists it is inconsistent F31-style: "Open checklist" vs "View this checklist on eBird" vs "Open eBird checklist S…". A screen-reader user who learns one identification on the Checklists tab cannot recognize the same function on Statistics or in a map popup, and sighted users get no stable visual signature for 'this opens the checklist' either.
evidence: WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111 `{id}` vs BirdingStats.tsx:1332 `↗` vs Checklists.tsx:54-62 `{formatDate(date)}` (no label) vs BirdingStats.tsx:500-505 date-only link with `textDecoration: 'none'` and no icon.
suggestedFix: Create one shared ChecklistLink component (extending the existing speciesDetail/ui.tsx StatValueLink, which already gates on SUBMISSION_ID_RE) with a single visual signature (ExternalLink icon) and one accessible-name formula (e.g. aria-label=`Open checklist ${id} on eBird` plus the new-tab suffix already used in NamedBirdRow). Replace all four variants — the ↗ glyphs, the unlabeled icon links, the plain-text links, and the title-only underlined ids — with it.

verdict.reasoning: All four variants verified at the cited lines: bare ↗ with title='Open checklist' (BirdingStats 1332/1564/1589), value+ExternalLink with no label (StatValueLink ui.tsx:52-78, DateLink Checklists.tsx:48-65) vs NamedBirdRow.tsx:90-100's full aria-label, plain accent text with textDecoration:'none' (BirdingStats 500/695/726/1448/1525, SightingsMap.tsx:62-75, TargetMarkers.tsx:104 — which is in fact a fifth vocabulary, 'View checklist S… →'), and underlined id with title='View this checklist on eBird' (WeatherTidePanel.tsx:108-111, ChecklistComparer.tsx:429-432). This is a genuine 3.2.4 inconsistent-identification issue whose root cause (no shared component or name formula) is distinct from confirmed #53 (↗ missing accessible name) and structure findings #4/#5 (new-window indication, title-attribute reliance), which the finding explicitly carves out. The suggested shared ChecklistLink keeps the SUBMISSION_ID_RE standing security check, consistent with conventions.

title: Dark theme: map pin tokens are lightened 'for dark backgrounds' but draw on the always-light Positron basemap (1.69–2.25:1)
description: There is no dark basemap variant (lib/mapStyle.ts tunes Positron only; no theme branch), yet the dark-theme --sr-map-* tokens lighten the pin colors: visited/heat pins #34D399 vs Positron land (~#F2F0EB) = 1.69:1, personal #E0A060 = 1.97:1, unvisited #7BA7C9 = 2.25:1 (light theme passes: 3.66–3.97:1). The GL circle/teardrop sprites read these tokens at runtime (map/SightingMarkers.tsx:80, lib/mapPins.ts, HotspotMarkers sprites), so switching the app to dark mode makes the primary map markers fainter against the unchanged light tiles. White glyphs inside the dark-theme teardrops also drop below 3:1 (star on #E0A060 = 2.24:1, dots on #7BA7C9 = 2.56:1). Mitigation: the sidebar in-view lists duplicate marker info, which keeps this from serious.
fix: Anchor the on-map pin tokens to the basemap, not the app theme (keep the light-theme values in dark mode, or add a dark halo/outline to the GL sprites); keep the lightened values only for sidebar legend dots that actually sit on dark surfaces.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the mechanism end-to-end: lib/mapStyle.ts has no dark basemap variant (Positron only), SightingMarkers.tsx reads --sr-map-visited via useCssToken at runtime (theme-reactive per the data-theme MutationObserver contract), and my recomputation matches exactly — dark tokens #34D399/#E0A060/#7BA7C9 hit 1.69/1.97/2.25:1 on ~#F2F0EB land, with white teardrop glyphs at 2.24/2.56; the pin strokes are hardcoded white (SightingMarkers.tsx:160, mapPins.ts:133) so they add no edge contrast on light tiles. One inaccuracy: light theme does NOT fully pass — --sr-map-personal #C9842A is only 2.70:1 on the land tint, so the personal pin fails 1.4.11 in both themes. ACCESSIBILITY.md documents the sidebar keyboard path to markers but not marker contrast, so not disclosed; the sidebar mitigation keeps moderate the right severity.
verdict.fixNote: Add dedicated basemap-anchored pin tokens (e.g. --sr-map-pin-*) defined with the SAME values in both :root and [data-theme="dark"] for the GL circle layer and sprite bakes, keeping the existing --sr-map-* for sidebar legend/list dots on app surfaces. Note 'keep the light-theme values' alone is insufficient: light --sr-map-personal #C9842A is itself 2.70:1 on the land tint, so pair the shared pin tokens with a dark stroke ring — replace the hardcoded #ffffff circle-stroke-color (SightingMarkers.tsx:160) and sprite strokeStyle '#fff' (mapPins.ts:133) with a dark outline to supply the 3:1 boundary against light tiles.

title: External links open new windows without any indication (inconsistent across the app)
description: 43 target="_blank" anchors exist across ~20 component files; only two indicate the behavior — App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 use "(opens in new tab)" in aria-label. All others give no warning, including every link in the Help documentation (HelpDocs.tsx:61 renders all HELP.md links with target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" and no indication), the footer GitHub link (App.tsx:1101-1110), SpeciesLinks.tsx:20/45 (whose aria-labels "View X on eBird" omit it), LifeListTable.tsx media-count links, BirdingStats.tsx checklist/region links (15 instances), Checklists.tsx, MapExplorer.tsx, SpeciesDetail.tsx, NamedBirdRow.tsx, Settings.tsx, WeatherTidePanel.tsx, MediaCommentsSection.tsx, MediaStatsSections.tsx, ChecklistComparer.tsx, SightingsMap.tsx, map/HotspotMarkers.tsx, map/TargetMarkers.tsx, AtlasLayer.tsx, speciesDetail/ui.tsx, CommentText.tsx. Unexpected context changes disorient screen-reader and cognitive-disability users; the app already has the right pattern in two places — it just isn't applied consistently.
evidence: HelpDocs.tsx:61 `<a key={ki++} href={lm[2]} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` with no new-window indication; grep shows 43 target="_blank" instances, only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 carry "(opens in new tab)".
suggestedFix: Adopt one shared ExternalA component (or extend SpeciesLinks' pattern) that appends "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name (visually-hidden span or aria-label suffix) and use it for all target="_blank" anchors, including HelpDocs' renderInline link branch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: exactly 43 target="_blank" anchors across 20 component files, with only App.tsx:748 and App.tsx:898 announcing '(opens in new tab)'; HelpDocs.tsx renders every documentation link target="_blank" with no indication and SpeciesLinks.tsx aria-labels omit it. This is the new-window-indication aspect, explicitly distinct from confirmed #53 (which covers the ↗ links' accessible names), so not a duplicate. Correctly scoped as advisory (G201; 3.2.5 is AAA), so minor severity is right; not disclosed in ACCESSIBILITY.md.
verdict.fixNote: A shared external-link component is sound; prefer a visually-hidden span suffix over aria-label so existing link text is preserved, and where an aria-label already exists (SpeciesLinks, icon-only links) append to the label, matching the wording already used at App.tsx:748/898. For icon-only favicon links keep title in sync with the label.

title: MapLibre attribution toggle is partially obscured to a 24×10 px target on every map (WCAG 2.2 target-size)
description: axe-core's target-size rule flagged the compact attribution control's <summary class="maplibregl-ctrl-attrib-button" aria-label="Toggle attribution"> in every runtime map state scanned (Map Explorer light and dark, with a popup open, in fullscreen, and behind the Help overlay): the button is nominally 24×24 but is partially obscured so its smallest unobstructed space is 24×10 px, below the 24×24 minimum. This is the keyboard/pointer target that expands the legally-required tile-provider credits. The element was present in the prior light scan's DOM but appears in no recorded finding (the prior 2.2 target-size findings i=67/75/85/86 cover favicon links, the combobox chevron, sidebar form controls, and a hotspot eBird link; raw finding notes mention the attribution font size and the AtlasLayer close button only).
evidence: axe target-size node, repeated across map states: html `<summary class="maplibregl-ctrl-attrib-button" title="Toggle attribution" aria-label="Toggle attribution"></summary>`, data `{"messageKey":"partiallyObscured","minSize":24,"width":24,"height":10}` — 'Target has insufficient size because it is partially obscured (smallest space is 24px by 10px, should be at least 24px by 24px)'. SnowMap.tsx:121 `attributionControl={{ compact: true }}`.
suggestedFix: Find what overlaps the bottom-right ctrl corner (the map container's bottom edge/rounding or the adjacent control margin) and add bottom clearance via CSS — e.g. a `.maplibregl-ctrl-bottom-right { margin-bottom: ... }` rule or padding on the map container — so the full 24×24 summary is exposed; verify with axe target-size on the Map Explorer afterward.

verdict.reasoning: The axe geometry checks out structurally: .sr-map-fab-cluster (globals.css:470 — bottom:20px, right:16px, z-index:1050, 36px-tall buttons) overlaps the compact attribution <summary> (24x24 at bottom-right with maplibre's 10px margin, occupying 10-34px from the bottom edge), leaving exactly the reported 24x10 unobscured strip. Scope correction: the fab cluster renders only in MapExplorer.tsx:1447, so this affects the Map Explorer map only, not 'every map' — all scanned states in the evidence were Map Explorer states. Real WCAG 2.2 target-size issue, distinct from the i=67/75/85/86 target-size findings; minor severity is right.
verdict.fixNote: The obscuring element is the .sr-map-fab-cluster (fullscreen/Filters FAB), not the map edge. Scope the fix to the Map Explorer: either move the attribution clear of the cluster (e.g. a Map Explorer-scoped `.maplibregl-ctrl-bottom-right { margin-right: 60px }` so the 24x24 summary clears the 36px FAB at right:16px) or render the AttributionControl bottom-left there; the other maps need no change.

title: Form-control borders are far below non-text contrast (1.19–1.34:1)
description: --sr-border (#E4E4E7 light / #27272A dark) is the only boundary cue on text inputs, selects, date inputs and unselected pills throughout the app (SELECT_STYLE here; the same '1px/1.5px solid var(--sr-border)' pattern on inputs in MapExplorer, Checklists, LifeList, Settings, SpeciesDetail). Computed: 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark vs surface, 1.21:1 / 1.34:1 vs page bg; even --sr-border-medium is 1.73:1 light / 1.70:1 dark. Inputs whose extent is identified only by this border fail 1.4.11; the focus ring fixes it only once focused.
fix: Introduce an --sr-border-input token at ≥3:1 vs surface (≈#949499 light, ≈#5F5F66 dark) for form-control boundaries, or give inputs a contrasting filled background (--sr-surface-subtle is itself only 1.07:1 vs surface, so the border route is simpler).

verdict.reasoning: Re-computed all ratios and they match: --sr-border vs surface is 1.27:1 light / 1.19:1 dark (1.21/1.34 vs page bg), --sr-border-medium 1.73/1.70 — the borders are near-invisible. But the W3C Understanding of 1.4.11 does not require a visible boundary when the control is otherwise identifiable, and every cited control carries a placeholder ('Search by place name', 'Paste your API key', 'e.g. 37.8275') and/or a visible label, and SELECT_STYLE selects show a ~4.7:1 chevron glyph — so this is a genuine low-vision usability weakness, not a clear normative AA failure. Confirmed as a worthwhile polish fix at minor severity rather than moderate.
verdict.fixNote: The --sr-border-input token approach is right (define in both :root and [data-theme="dark"]), but the suggested dark value #5F5F66 is only 2.80:1 vs --sr-surface #18181B — below the fix's own 3:1 target. Use ~#6B6B73 (3.35:1) or #707078 (3.61:1) for dark; light #949499 passes at 3.02:1 but only barely, so a slightly darker value gives margin.

title: Inline `outline: 'none'` on ~20 inputs/selects suppresses the designed focus ring app-wide
description: One repeated pattern: form controls styled with inline `outline: 'none'`, which overrides the global input ring (globals.css:556-563, `outline: 2px solid var(--sr-accent)`). The only surviving indicator is the rule's `border-color: var(--sr-accent) !important` (stylesheet !important still beats inline) plus a 12%-alpha shadow — a 1.5px gray→green border tint instead of the designed 2px ring, easy to miss in dense filter sidebars, and weaker than ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs'. Locations: lib/mapExplorerFormat.ts:27 (SELECT_STYLE shared by all Map Explorer selects); MapExplorer.tsx:88,690,692,863,865,1184; LifeList.tsx:627,653,667; BreedingCodeList.tsx:388,419,435; SpeciesDetail.tsx:518,613,638,652,1273; Checklists.tsx:170,265; MediaCommentsSection.tsx:75; Settings.tsx:435,1219,1231,1243. Technically still a visible state change (so not a hard 2.4.7 fail), but a significant app-wide degradation versus the global design.
fix: Remove every inline `outline: 'none'` from inputs/selects — the global stylesheet already suppresses the default ring on non-focus-visible states and supplies the 2px accent ring on focus. The per-element onFocus borderColor handlers (e.g. Settings.tsx:437) become redundant and can stay or go.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all claims: 26 inline outline:'none' occurrences match the listed locations, inline style beats the non-!important outline in globals.css:556-563, and only the !important border-color plus the stylesheet box-shadow survive — the designed 2px ring never renders on these controls. However the surviving indicator (1.5px border flipping gray→accent at 4.52:1 light / 9.22:1 dark vs surface, plus a 4px glow, with explicit onFocus borderColor handlers in Settings) is a perceivable, conventional focus treatment, so 2.4.7 AA is not actually failed — the finding itself concedes this. Real as an app-wide design-consistency issue that also makes ACCESSIBILITY.md's published 'border-hugging ring on inputs' claim inaccurate, but a non-failing degradation grades as minor, not moderate.
